ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the JsonProperty annotation of an enum value: hops 3 and 4 pass the value through unchanged, hop 2 keys the gold's non-null results by Enum.name(), and hop 1 overwrites the entries of names that have a key, leaving the others unmodified. The gold's javadoc promises the name the annotation gives to the value; a constant with a class body is an instance of an anonymous subclass that declares no field, so the field that declares it is found only in the formal enum type, and once the gold has returned null for such a value no caller can recover the name without re-reading the annotation or replacing the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: ClassUtil.findEnumType(Enum) and findEnumType(Class) climb from a class body to the formal type ('enums with body are sub-classes of the formal type'), EnumValues.constructFromName applies it before calling the facade ('Enum types with per-instance sub-classes need special handling'), and the deprecated sibling JacksonAnnotationIntrospector.findEnumValue reads the constant's field with Class.getField, which searches the superclass. testEnumsWithJsonProperty (an annotated plain constant) and both testSubclassedEnums (constants with bodies, no annotation) pass through the chain; ClassUtilTest.testFindEnumType pins the helper.
